headline: Approved a partial lane closure on Whitney Avenue for Halloween and an accessible parking space at 103 Gorham Avenue.
summary: Residents wrote about speeding, a traffic light request, and a block party. Members approved the September 14, 2026 minutes, a partial lane closure on Whitney Avenue for Halloween, and an accessible parking space at 103 Gorham Avenue. They also moved a Glenbrook Avenue speed hump request to the traffic-calming list.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the September 14, 2026 regular meeting, unanimous.
Approved a partial lane closure on Whitney Avenue for Halloween, requested from the State CT DOT, unanimous.
Approved an accessible parking space request for 103 Gorham Avenue, unanimous.
Moved the Glenbrook Avenue speed hump request to the traffic-calming list, unanimous.

Commissioner Zachery made a motion to approve item 9a. Commissioner King seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in favor.
Commissioner King made a motion to move item 9b to the traffic-calming list. Commissioner White seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in favor.

TOWN OF HAMDEN, CONNECTICUT 
 
Traffic Authority Minutes         
         
Regular Meeting 
 
5:30 PM, October 19, 2026 
 
 
 
Hamden Government 
Center 
2nd Floor Conference 
Room 
2750 Dixwell Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
Tel:  (203) 287-7070 
Fax:  (203) 287-7075 
 Click to View Agenda   
  
1. CALL TO ORDER 
  
 Chairman Willis called the Traffic Authority's regular meeting to order at 5:35 PM 
2. ATTENDANCE 
  
 The Traffic Authority Clerk, Nancy Forvil, took a roll call. Commissioner's present: Willis, 
White, Zachery, King, Hampton. 
 
Staff: LTA, Stephen White. 
3. PUBLIC COMMENT 
  
 Sarah Clark  
4. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES 
  
 
 
  a. Approval of minutes of the Traffic Authority's regular meetings on September 14, 
2026.  
  Commissioner Hampton made a motion to approve the regular meeting minutes of 
September 14, 2026. Commissioner King seconded the motion. The vote was 
unanimous in favor. 
5. CORRESPONDENCE 
There will be a brief summary of the correspondence submitted between the last 
correspondence update and this one. This includes but is not limited to any 
correspondence with council members that members wish to submit for the record. It can 
also include written communication to the council from the administration, community 
members, etc.   
 
 
  a. John Murphy, 253 Augur Street — Traffic-calming request on Augur Street or speed 
hump installation, the stop sign is ignored by motorists.
b. Dorette Fowlin, 50 Bradley Avenue — Neighborhood concerns about speeding in 
general on a regular basis. Dog was killed, cars have been damaged (hit & run) and a 
child was struck between Duane Street and Bradley Avenue. School is close by and 
many children walk or ride bicycles to school because the bus doesn't pick up on 
Bradley Avenue due to proximity to the school (Helen Street School). Speed humps 
on the roadway would go a long way on slowing down the motorists.  
  
 
  c. Marylou Weinzimmer — I am writing to formally request the installation of a traffic 
light on the corner of Todd Street and Whitney Avenue. This intersection experiences 
heavy traffic throughout the day, especially work traffic. It is impossible in the morning 
and late afternoon to take a left onto Whitney. As one side clears, the other side fills 
up, and you are just in a holding pattern with cars piling up on Todd Street. I also feel 
this will slow traffic down, especially during school season, as the students from 
Quinnipiac are trying to cross and walk on Whitney, which is obviously so dangerous 
and unsafe for all. Thank you for your consideration and I look forward to hearing a 
response.  
  
 
  d. SILDA NOLASCO, 80 NOBLE ST—I am writing as a resident of 80 Noble Street in 
Hamden to bring an important traffic and pedestrian safety concern to your attention 
regarding the park located directly in front of my home. 
 
Since moving to this residence, I have become increasingly concerned about the 
speed at which some vehicles travel through this area. The entrance to the park and 
the street are very close to one another, and children frequently run, walk, and play in 
and around the park. At times, I have personally observed vehicles traveling fast 
enough that drivers have had to stop suddenly when children were near or crossing 
the street. Because the park is used by children and families, I believe additional 
traffic-safety measures could help make the area safer. I respectfully ask the Town to 
consider installing slow-down signs, children-at-play signs, pedestrian crossing signs, 
or other appropriate traffic-control measures near the park to alert drivers that they 
are entering an area where children and pedestrians are frequently present. I am also 
concerned about the number of vehicles that remain parked in the area for extended 
periods, including while children and families are using the park. The park includes a 
public restroom, and some individuals appear to use the area for extended periods, 
including sleeping in their vehicles. This has made some parents and families 
uncomfortable while bringing their children to the park. 
 
I understand that the park is a public space and that everyone has the right to use it. 
My concern is primarily the safety and comfort of the children and families who use 
the park, particularly because the street and park entrance are so close together. As 
a parent and a new resident of the neighborhood, I find it difficult to feel comfortable 
allowing my children to play at the park or cross the street to access it when vehicles 
are traveling at high speeds. A public park intended for children should be a place 
where families can feel safe and comfortable. I respectfully ask the Town of Hamden 
to please evaluate this area and consider whether additional signage, traffic-calming 
measures, pedestrian safety improvements, or increased enforcement may be 
appropriate. I believe taking preventive action now could help avoid a serious 
accident or injury in the future. Thank you for taking the time to consider my concerns 
and for helping make our neighborhood safer for children, families, pedestrians, and
drivers. I would greatly appreciate any assistance or information regarding what steps 
can be taken to address this situation. 
 
 
  
  
 
  e. The engineering department is requesting a partial lane closure on Whitney Avenue from the 
State CT DOT for traffic safety during Halloween.  
  Commissioner White made a motion to move correspondence 5e to new business for 
a vote. Commissioner Hampton seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in 
favor. 
 
Commissioner King made a motion to approve correspondence 5e in new business. 
Commissioner Hampton seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in favor. 
  f. Douglas Foley - Block party request, Doren Avenue, October 23, 2026, rain date 
10/24/2026, 3:00PM-8:00PM  
  
 
  g. Jennie Ragan — We are wondering if there was any further information about traffic-
calming requests in the town. We have lived on Riverside Drive since 2014. Over the 
course of that time, the speeding coming directly down Riverside Drive and off of the 
side streets has gotten progressively worse.  We’ve come to the point where we are 
very hesitant to even take a walk with our children on bikes or scooters in the 
neighborhood because of how fast the traffic has become. We are very concerned 
that there is going to be an accident and somebody is going to get hurt and have 
personally had close calls with speeding vehicles. We think the road would be a very 
good candidate for a traffic study and imagine we’d be able to get the required 
number of signatures if submission was still allowed or would be considered on a 
case by case basis. Please let us know if you have any further information on how we 
might be able to improve the safety in the neighborhood.  
  
 
  h. Karen L. Butler, Helen Street School —Requesting a temporary, 1-hour road closure 
for our annual Ruby Bridges Day celebration and parade on Friday, November 13th; 
section of Helen Street between Langer Street and Pine Rock Avenue from 2:00 PM 
to 3:00 PM.  
  Commissioner Hampton made a motion to move correspondence 5h to new business 
for a vote. Commissioner Zachery seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in 
favor. 
 
Commissioner King made a motion to approve correspondence 5e in new business. 
Commissioner Hampton seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in favor. 
6. REPORTS 
  
 Presented by LTA, Stephen White. 
7. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommended by the town attorney)
There was no executive session. 
8. OLD BUSINESS 
  
 There was no old business. 
9. NEW BUSINESS 
  
 
 
  a. Tyrell Tyson, 103 Gorham Avenue — Accessible parking space approval request.  
  Commissioner Zachery made a motion to approve item 9a. Commissioner King 
seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in favor. 
  b. Glenbrook Avenue Residents - Speed hump request on Glenbrook Avenue. Motorists 
are speeding, hitting parked cars and utility poles. Residents are worried about the 
children who play in the neighborhood.  
  Commissioner King made a motion to move item 9b to the traffic-calming list. 
Commissioner White seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in favor. 
10. ADJOURNMENT 
  
 There being no further business to discuss, Commissioner Hampton made a motion to adjourn 
the Traffic Authority regular meeting. Commissioner King seconded the motion. The vote was 
unanimous in favor. The meeting adjourned at 6:11 PM.

1. CALL TO ORDER   
 Chairman Willis called the Traffic Authority's regular meeting to order at 5:35 PM 
2. ATTENDANCE   
 The Traffic Authority Clerk, Nancy Forvil, took a roll call. Commissioner's present: Willis, 
White, Zachery, Jones, Hampton and Ladore. 
 
Staff: Stehen White, Town Engineer and LTA. 
3. PUBLIC COMMENT   
 LaShawn Jefferson 
4. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES   
 
 
  a. Approval of minutes of the Traffic Authority's regular meetings on July 13th and 
August 10, 2026.  
  Commissioner Zachery made a motion to approve the regular meeting minutes of July 
13th and August 10, 2026.. Commissioner Jones seconded the motion. The vote was 
unanimous in favor. 
5. CORRESPONDENCE 
There will be a brief summary of the correspondence submitted between the last 
correspondence update and this one. This includes but is not limited to any 
correspondence with council members that members wish to submit for the record. It can 
also include written communication to the council from the administration, community 
members, etc.   
 
 
  a. Janet Kazienko, 32 Fern Street - Block party request, between Wood & Mather, 9/26 
3:00PM-7:00PM, rain date 9/27  
  Commissioner Hampton made a motion to approve item 5a. Commissioner Jones 
seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in favor. 
  b. Tyrell Tyson, 103 Gorham Avenue — Accessible parking space approval request.
c. Glenbrook Avenue Residents - Speed hump request on Glenbrook Avenue. Motorists 
are speeding, hitting parked cars and utility poles. Residents are worried about the 
children who play in the neighborhood.  
  
 
6. REPORTS   
 
 
7. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommended by the town attorney)  
 There was no executive session. 
8. OLD BUSINESS   
 
 
  a. Robert B. Cochran, 687 Ridge Road— I would like to petition the city to install a 
crosswalk at this important intersection (Ridge Rd, Hartford Tpke, and Robinwood 
Rd). My wife and infant daughter and I live nearby and frequently cross this busy 
intersection on walks, and being forced to cross without any crosswalk (despite 
several sidewalks leading up to it!) creates a great deal of anxiety and is frankly 
unsafe. Given that the intersection lies in a scenic neighborhood, near a park, and 
along a route regularly used by the New Haven Bike Club, we frequently see other 
walkers, runners, and bicyclists also contending with the same problem.  
  Commissioner White made a motion to refer item 8a to the traffic department to install 
crosswalk infrastructure when funding is available between Ridge Road and Hartford 
Turnpike. Commissioner Hampton seconded the motion. 
  b. Stephanie Profenna, 29 Myra Road—There’s a huge intersection by the firehouse on 
Hartford Turnpike and Ridge Road. With incoming traffic around the corner, it’s hard 
to cross the street from the dog park or children’s playground towards the firehouse. 
I’m often walking with my baby and dog in tow and don’t always feel safe crossing 
that road.  
  Commissioner White made a motion to refer item 8b to the traffic department to install 
crosswalk infrastructure when funding is available between Ridge Road and Hartford 
Turnpike. Commissioner Hampton seconded the motion. 
  c. Eda Bozdemir, 137 Hepburn Road — Please add a crosswalk to this area for safety. 
(Ridge Rd, Hartford Turnpike, and Robinwood Rd)  
  Commissioner White made a motion to refer item 8c to the traffic department to install 
crosswalk infrastructure when funding is available between Ridge Road and Hartford 
Turnpike. Commissioner Hampton seconded the motion. 
9. NEW BUSINESS   
 
 
  a. Joan King I would like to know how we can improve the safety and extremely 
excessive auto noise on Ridge Rd and Hartford Tnpk, the streets surrounding the 
Coptic Church (formerly St Stephen’s) in our neighborhood.  I have complained to the 
police and nothing changes.  The cars are exceptionally loud, and they tear down 
Ridge and Hartford Turnpike at extremely dangerous high speeds throughout the day 
and late at night, especially Friday–Sunday.  The cars park and gather in the Coptic
Church lot.   We’re afraid there will be a tragic accident.   The traffic-calming islands 
do not stop them in the least.   Speed humps might be more effective, traffic cameras 
and police enforcement.   I’ve called the police numerous times. Nothing changes. 
This is ongoing, every week.  No one seems to care to do anything about it.  It has 
kept us up at nights and very distressed.  We are a quiet residential neighborhood.  I 
know this has been on the books for a long while now. It’s very discouraging. Is there 
anything more that can be done?  Speed humps? Speed Cameras and 
enforcement?  Is anyone else proposing these changes and improvements?  
  Commissioner White made a motion to refer item 9a to the traffic department for a 
traffic study on a portion of Ridge Road and review the weekend parking lot activity. 
Commissioner Ladore seconded the motion. 
  10. ADJOURNMENT  
 There being no further business to discuss, Commissioner Ladore made a motion to adjourn 
the Traffic Authority regular meeting. Commissioner Hampton seconded the motion. The vote 
was unanimous in favor. The meeting adjourned at 5:51 PM.
